Written by the DSL course sync from templates/site/ in the # toolkit; every sync rewrites it. layout: page --- {{ content }} {% comment %} Your Profile - the settings that let every other page offer a file in the student's own copy (see _includes/open_in.html, which owns the URL rules and is included below so that this page's own buttons derive a path exactly the way a file row does). One static page, no back end: the site is public and identical for everybody, so what it learns here it keeps in the reader's own browser (localStorage) and sends nowhere. Nothing is stored until a Save is pressed, and every button below step 1 reads the SAVED values, not what is currently in a box - a half-typed path that enabled a button would open the wrong folder and look like the page's fault. One Save per field, beside its own box, with what it stored on the line underneath. The box always holds something editable: the saved value, or until there is one the field's example (its placeholder, respelt for the reader's platform below) - so a student edits `j.doe` into their own name rather than retyping a whole path over a grey hint that goes at the first keystroke. Save stores what is in the box and leaves it there. An empty box, or the untouched example, plus Save is a no-op rather than a delete or a saved example; `clear` on the saved line is how a setting is removed, and it puts the example back. Four numbered steps, in the order they have to happen: details, fork, clone, open. Step 3 stays greyed until step 2 has been taken, because cloning a fork that does not exist yet is the one failure mode with no useful error at the other end - the editor just reports a repository it cannot find. "Mark this step done" is the way out for a student who forked last term, or on another machine: the flag is this browser's, not GitHub's, and the page cannot ask GitHub without sending the reader's handle somewhere. Step 3 can only NAME the folder to clone into: `vscode://vscode.git/clone` carries a url and a ref and nothing else, so a student who accepts whatever folder the dialog opens at leaves step 4 - and every `local` button on the site - pointing at a clone that is not there. Under it is the command that needs no dialog: the page cannot RUN anything, but the line it prints puts the clone exactly where the folder above says it is - and works for a student whose editor is not VS Code, who gets no clone button at all. The materials repo is named once here, as the default a cohort release deploys into (`cohort_dest_repo`, dsl_course/deploy.py). Nothing else on this page depends on it: the per-file control reads the repo out of each file's own GitHub URL, so a course that renamed its materials repo still gets working file links and only these buttons point at the default name. The two folder examples put the clone under a folder named for THIS cohort org, so a student on two courses is not steered into cloning two `materials` repos into one place. They ship spelt as macOS spells a home folder, and the script below respells the home part for the reader's own platform where the browser can tell (Windows, Linux) - a Windows student shown `/Users/j.doe/...` typed it in verbatim and got a path no editor could open. {% endcomment %}
